title: Circular-mode optics for high-intensity beams and high-luminosity colliders
metadata_source.abstract: <jats:p>We study circular-mode optics as a framework for transporting and accelerating intrinsically flat beams while maintaining a round transverse projection in physical space. Motivated by the strong degradation of flat beams under low-energy space-charge forces, we develop a coupled-optics description of circular modes, analyze their formation and preservation, and derive lattice design conditions for conserving canonical angular momentum and coupling phase. These conditions motivate rotationally invariant transport and ring cells based on solenoids, symmetric alternating-gradient structures, and indexed dipoles. We further derive space-charge tune-shift and tune-spread expressions for circular-mode beams in uncoupled and coupled lattices, showing that they preserve the leading-order space-charge behavior of round beams while retaining intrinsic eigenemittance flatness. Particle-in-cell simulations with TRACK and mpact confirm the generation, transport, and acceleration of circular-mode beams in representative lattices, including regimes with strong space charge. Circular-mode optics therefore provides a promising route toward high-intensity hadron beams and high-luminosity collider applications.</jats:p>

title: Pyrolysis-Dependent Uncollided Neutron Transmission in Date-Palm Biochar/Epoxy Composites: A GEANT4 Study with 2 MeV and Cf-252 Neutrons

affiliation.name: Department of Physics, College of Science, Qassim University, Buraydah 51452, Qassim, Saudi Arabia

metadata_source.abstract: <jats:p>Pyrolysis changes both the composition and physical structure of biochar, making it necessary to separate chemistry-driven neutron-transport effects from density and geometry effects. This computational study examines date-palm biochars produced at 300, 500, and 800 °C as fillers in an idealized epoxy matrix. The principal 2 MeV comparison used ten independent 106-history GEANT4 runs per material at 20 wt% filler, 5 cm thickness, and equal bulk density (1.25 g cm−3). From BC300 to BC800, total forward track-length fluence increased by only 0.30%, whereas the fluence-weighted H∗(10) response increased by 2.86%. A separate ten-replicate component campaign confirmed that the 2 MeV BC800–BC300 H∗(10) difference (+0.07986 pSv primary−1) was driven by increased uncollided-primary transmission (+0.08398 pSv primary−1), while the collided-primary contribution decreased slightly (−0.00422 pSv primary−1). For a representative 252Cf Watt spectrum, H∗(10) increased by 2.98%, with 91.1% of the net increase arising from uncollided primaries. A 30×30 cm2 full-face geometry increased scattered buildup, yet 84.0% of the BC800–BC300 H∗(10) increase remained attributable to uncollided primaries. Additional density, thickness, and loading sensitivities gave positive BC800–BC300 H∗(10) contrasts under all tested conditions (1.18–8.24%), although the integral-fluence contrast was not universally positive. The model therefore supports a robust chemistry-related increase in high-energy primary survival while showing that the scattered-field partition and engineering performance remain geometry- and processing-dependent.</jats:p>

citation_title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
citation_abstract: $^{99m}$Tc [t$_{1/2}$=6.0072 h, IT: 99.9963%, E_${\gamma}$=140.51 keV (89%)] is the most widely used radionuclide for SPECT imaging. It is mainly obtained from $^{99}$Mo/$^{99m}$Tc generators, with $^{99}$Mo [t$_{1/2}$=65.924 h, $\beta^{-}$:100%] produced by fission of $^{235}$U in nuclear reactors. The aging of reactors dedicated to $^{99}$Mo production and increasingly frequent maintenance shutdowns highlight the need for alternative production routes. Among accelerator-based approaches, direct production of $^{99m}$Tc from enriched $^{100}$Mo targets using low-energy proton beams is particularly promising. Within a collaboration between the Laboratory for High Energy Physics (LHEP) of the University of Bern and the Department of Nuclear and High Energy Physics of Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, we investigated $^{99m}$Tc production with medical cyclotrons. Cross sections of proton-induced reactions on solid molybdenum targets were measured to characterise the Tc radionuclides produced during irradiation and optimise production conditions. Based on these data, a proton energy of approximately 16 MeV and a highly enriched $^{100}$Mo target of about 0.5 mm thickness were identified as suitable conditions. For a 10 h irradiation, these parameters provide a calculated $^{99m}$Tc yield of approximately 1.7 GBq/$\mu$A while maintaining radionuclidic purity within European Pharmacopoeia limits. Production tests were subsequently performed to validate the measurements and demonstrate the feasibility of this production route.

                  <jats:p>

However, the identification of reconnection within turbulence remains a significant challenge. To automatically detect magnetic reconnection in plasma turbulence, we propose a novel and efficient classifier called a dual-branch lightweight hybrid convolutional neural network (DHCNN), which, for the first time, achieves automatic localization of reconnection sites by effectively leveraging negative-valued information in physical variables.
